section.content: 本发明提供锂离子电池电解液、锂离子电池、锂离子电池组及锂离子电池包，涉及锂离子电池制备技术领域。一种锂离子电池电解液，包括氢氟醚、锂盐，氢氟醚占电解液质量百分比为30％～36％，锂盐占电解液质量百分比为20％～25％，锂盐选自双氟磺酰亚胺锂或双三氟磺酰亚胺锂中的至少一种。锂离子电池电解液与硅碳负极材料之间的副反应较小，粘度、密度较小，离子电导率高，因此，由电解液制备的电芯的电化学性能和循环稳定性优异。

The invention provides lithium ion battery electrolyte, a lithium ion battery pack and a lithium ion battery pack, and relates to the technical field of lithium ion battery preparation. The lithium ion battery electrolyte comprises 30-36% of hydrofluoroether and 20-25% of lithium salt, wherein the lithium salt is at least one of lithium bis (fluorosulfonyl) imide or lithium bis (trifluorosulfonyl) imide. The lithium ion battery electrolyte has small side reaction with the silicon-carbon negative electrode material, small viscosity and density and high ion conductivity, so that the electrochemical performance and the cycling stability of the battery cell prepared by the electrolyte are excellent.

Lithium ion battery electrolyte, lithium ion battery pack and lithium ion battery packTechnical Field

The invention relates to the technical field of lithium ion battery preparation, in particular to lithium ion battery electrolyte, a lithium ion battery pack and a lithium ion battery pack.

Background

The lithium ion battery is a battery with high energy density, light weight and environmental protection, and is widely applied to the fields of mobile power supplies, electric vehicles, unmanned aerial vehicles, intelligent wearing and the like. Among them, the negative electrode material is one of the keys determining the battery performance. The cathode material of the traditional lithium ion battery is graphite, has lower theoretical specific capacity and longer charge and discharge time, and limits the energy density and the cycle life of the battery. The high specific energy lithium ion power battery using the silicon-carbon composite material as the negative electrode has higher theoretical specific capacity, and is expected to greatly improve the energy density and the power density of the battery.

However, the silicon-carbon composite material has the problems of capacity fading, volume expansion and the like, and the electrolyte with higher performance is required to be matched with the silicon-carbon composite material so as to weaken the capacity fading, volume expansion and the like caused by the silicon-carbon composite material. The conventional high-performance commercial lithium ion battery electrolyte comprises a main solvent of carbonic ester and lithium salt with the mass ratio of 9% -13%, and although the electrolyte improves the performance of the battery to a certain extent, the electrolyte cannot inhibit side reactions with silicon-carbon anode materials. In order to inhibit side reactions with the silicon-carbon anode material, the prior proposal is to change the solvation structure of the electrolyte by increasing the concentration of lithium salt to more than 40 mass percent of the lithium salt in the electrolyte so as to reduce the reactivity between the electrolyte and the anode material. However, increasing the mass percentage of the lithium salt in the electrolyte can result in too high viscosity of the electrolyte, so that the electrochemical performance and the cycling stability of the battery cell are poor and the cost is too high.

Disclosure of Invention

(One) solving the technical problems

Aiming at the defects of the prior art, the invention provides lithium ion battery electrolyte, a lithium ion battery pack and a lithium ion battery pack, and solves the technical problem of larger side reaction between the existing lithium ion battery electrolyte and a silicon-carbon negative electrode material.

(II) technical scheme

In order to achieve the above purpose, the invention is realized by the following technical scheme:

In a first aspect, the invention provides lithium ion battery electrolyte, which comprises 30-36% of hydrofluoroether and 20-25% of lithium salt, wherein the lithium salt is at least one of lithium bis (fluorosulfonyl) imide or lithium bis (trifluorosulfonyl) imide.

The lithium ion battery electrolyte comprises hydrofluoroether and lithium salt, wherein the lithium salt accounts for 20-25% of the electrolyte by mass, the hydrofluoroether is used as a non-solvent, and does not participate in dissociation of the lithium salt, but is mutually dissolved with other solvents (carbonate, sulfate, carboxylate, phosphate, ether and the like), so that anions (lithium ions and the like) and cations (hexafluorophosphate ions, difluorosulfimide ions and the like) in the electrolyte form a solvation structure with good solvent (cyclic carbonate, cyclic sulfate, cyclic carboxylate, cyclic phosphate and the like) molecules, the solvation structure of the electrolyte can realize the solvation structure of the electrolyte when the lithium salt accounts for 40% of the electrolyte by mass when the lithium salt accounts for only 20-25% of the electrolyte by mass, and therefore, free solvent molecules in the electrolyte are reduced, the electrolyte contacts with the surface of an electrode and reacts less chance, thereby reducing side reactions between the electrolyte and a silicon-carbon negative electrode material, and the electrolyte has low electrochemical density, and the electrolyte core has low electrochemical density and good electrochemical cycle performance. And when the lithium salt is selected from one or two of lithium bis (fluorosulfonyl) imide and lithium bis (trifluorosulfonyl) imide as main salts, the compact anion-cation pair (Closed-shall ionpair, CIP) formed by the change of the solvation structure can react on the surface of the electrode to form an SEI layer with higher lithium fluoride content, and the substance is considered to be a more ideal SEI component, has better ion trafficability, electrochemistry and chemical stability, and can also improve the mechanical strength of a network SEI layer formed by ring-opening crosslinking of fluorovinylene carbonate. When the lithium salt is selected from one or two of lithium bis (fluorosulfonyl) imide and lithium bis (trifluorosulfonyl) imide as the main salt, the required lithium salt concentration can be easily achieved, and the phenomenon of precipitation of the lithium salt due to supersaturation at low temperature is not easy to occur, so that the low-temperature stability of the battery cell is improved.

As a preferred embodiment, the electrolyte further comprises a film forming additive, wherein the film forming additive accounts for 0.5% -5.0% of the electrolyte in percentage by mass, and the structural formula of the film forming additive is shown as formula (1):

Wherein in formula (I), R 1～R3 is each independently selected from any of substituted or unsubstituted C 1～C6 alkyl, substituted or unsubstituted C 1～C4 alkynyl, phosphate, amino, cyano, or substituted or unsubstituted C 6～C12 aryl, and hydrogen on alkyl, alkynyl, and aryl may be optionally substituted with halogen.

The film-forming additive has high reduction resistance, and can ensure that the film-forming additive is not consumed by reaction on the negative electrode side. The fluoro sulfonyl group can be oxidized at the positive electrode side under higher potential to form a Solid-electrolyte interface phase (SEI) with a protective effect, so that the positive electrode can be prevented from being attacked by free acid in the electrolyte, other components of the electrolyte are prevented from being oxidized at the positive electrode side, and nickel dissolution is inhibited. The silane groups in the film-forming additive can capture free acid in the electrolyte, and prevent the free acid from reacting with fluoroethylene carbonate with higher content in the electrolyte to generate hydrofluoric acid, so that corrosion of SEI on the surfaces of positive and negative electrode particles is avoided, and the service life of a battery is prolonged.

As a preferred embodiment, in the formula (I), each R 1～R3 is independently selected from any of substituted or unsubstituted C 1～C3 alkyl, unsubstituted C 1～C4 alkynyl, phosphate, amino, cyano, or unsubstituted C 6～C12 aryl, and hydrogen on the alkyl group may be optionally substituted with halogen.

As a preferred embodiment, in the formula (I), each R 1～R3 is independently selected from any one of methyl, ethyl, tert-butyl, perfluoromethyl, ethynyl, phosphate, amino, cyano or phenyl, so that the film forming additive containing the substituent group has a stronger binding effect on the free acid, thereby improving the cycle capacity retention rate and the cycle stability of the lithium ion battery.

As a preferred embodiment, the electrolyte further comprises a diluent, the diluent is selected from the group consisting of 1, 2-tetrafluoroethyl-2, 3-tetrafluoropropyl ether, 1, 2-tetrafluoroethyl ethyl ether, 1- (1, 2-tetrafluoroethoxy) propane one or more of 2, 2-trifluoroethyl ether, 1, 2-tetrafluoroethyl-2, 2-trifluoroethyl ether, 2-methyl-1- (1, 2-tetrafluoroethoxy) propane, the mass percentage of the diluent in the electrolyte is 30% -40%.

As a preferred embodiment, the electrolyte further includes an auxiliary additive, where the auxiliary additive is selected from one or more of vinylene carbonate, lithium difluorophosphate, lithium difluorooxalato borate, vinyl sulfate, cyclic sulfite, tri (trimethylsilyl) borate, tri (trimethylsilyl) phosphate or fluoroethylene carbonate, and the auxiliary additive accounts for 0.1% -5% of the electrolyte by mass, and more preferably, the auxiliary additive accounts for 0.5% -1.5% of the electrolyte by mass of the lithium ion battery, so that the cycle performance, low-temperature performance and flame retardant effect of the lithium ion battery can be further improved, and the electrochemical performance and cycle performance of the lithium ion battery can be further improved.

As a preferred embodiment, the lithium salt further includes one or more of lithium hexafluorophosphate, lithium tetrafluoroborate, lithium bisoxalato borate.

As a preferred embodiment, the electrolyte further includes an organic solvent, where the organic solvent is selected from one or more of ethylene carbonate, fluoroethylene carbonate, propylene carbonate, methyl ethyl carbonate, dimethyl carbonate, butylene carbonate, diethyl carbonate, propyl acetate, ethyl propionate, or propyl propionate, and the organic solvent accounts for 5% -50% of the electrolyte by mass.

As a preferred embodiment, the hydrofluoroether is 1, 2-tetrafluoroethyl-2, 3-tetrafluoropropyl ether, and the preferable dosage is 30% -36% of the electrolyte mass, so as to improve the ionic conductivity of the lithium ion electrolyte, thereby improving the electrochemical performance and the cycle stability of the lithium ion battery.

In a second aspect, the invention also provides a lithium ion battery, which comprises a silicon-based negative electrode material, a ternary positive electrode material and an electrolyte, wherein the electrolyte is the lithium ion battery electrolyte of the first aspect. For the reasons described above, the lithium ion battery exhibits excellent electrochemical performance, cycle stability, and higher cycle capacity retention.

The silicon-based negative electrode material can be a nano silicon negative electrode, a silicon-oxygen negative electrode, a silicon-carbon negative electrode or a silicon alloy negative electrode, and the ternary positive electrode material can be nickel-cobalt-manganese ternary materials (such as NCM111, NCM523, NCM622 or NCM 811) and nickel-cobalt-aluminum (NCA) materials with various nickel contents.

In a third aspect, the present invention also provides a lithium ion battery pack comprising the lithium ion battery of the second aspect. The lithium ion battery pack has higher energy density and can provide higher capacity and voltage.

In a fourth aspect, the present invention also provides a lithium ion battery pack comprising the lithium ion battery pack of the third aspect. The lithium ion battery pack can realize higher energy storage and release, and has higher safety performance.

Detailed Description

For the purpose of making the objects, technical solutions and advantages of the embodiments of the present invention more clear, the technical solutions in the embodiments of the present invention are clearly and completely described, and it is obvious that the described embodiments are some embodiments of the present invention, but not all embodiments. All other embodiments, which can be made by those skilled in the art based on the embodiments of the invention without making any inventive effort, are intended to be within the scope of the invention.

The embodiment of the application solves the technical problem of larger side reaction between the traditional lithium ion battery electrolyte and the silicon-carbon negative electrode material by providing the lithium ion battery electrolyte, the lithium ion battery pack and the lithium ion battery pack, and realizes the technical effects of excellent electrochemical performance and cycling stability and low cost of the battery cell prepared by the electrolyte.

The technical scheme in the embodiment of the application aims to solve the technical problems, and the overall thought is as follows:

In the existing lithium ion battery, the silicon-based anode material is repeatedly broken due to severe volume expansion in the charge and discharge process, and an interface-electrolyte intermediate phase (SEI) with a protective effect is formed on the surface of the anode material in the formation stage of the battery core, so that side reaction is continuously generated between the electrolyte and the anode material, and finally the problem of poor cycle performance of the lithium ion battery is caused, and the improvement of the mass percent of lithium salt in the electrolyte can reduce the reactivity between the electrolyte and the anode material, but the viscosity of the electrolyte is too high, so that the electrochemical performance and the cycle stability of the battery core are reduced, and the cost is too high.

In order to solve the problem, the lithium ion battery electrolyte comprises 20-25% of hydrofluoroether and lithium salt, wherein the lithium salt accounts for 20-25% of the electrolyte in percentage by mass, the hydrofluoroether is added while the concentration of the lithium salt is low, and the solvation structure is adjusted to reduce the reaction activity between the electrolyte and an electrode, so that the side reaction between the electrolyte and a silicon-carbon negative electrode material is reduced.

In addition, the lithium ion battery electrolyte also comprises a film forming additive, and the film forming additive has the structure as follows:

Wherein each R 1～R3 is independently selected from substituted or unsubstituted C 1～C6 alkyl, substituted or unsubstituted C 1～C4 alkynyl, phosphate, amino, cyano, or substituted or unsubstituted C 6～C12 aryl, and the hydrogens on the alkyl, alkynyl, and aryl groups may be optionally substituted with halogen. The film-forming additive has high reduction resistance, and can ensure that the film-forming additive is not consumed by reaction on the negative electrode side. The fluoro sulfonyl group can be oxidized at the positive electrode side under higher potential to form a solid phase-electrolyte interface phase (SEI-electrolyte inter-phase, SEI) with a protective effect, so that the positive electrode can be prevented from being attacked by free acid in the electrolyte, other components of the electrolyte are prevented from being oxidized at the positive electrode side, and nickel dissolution is inhibited. The silane groups in the film-forming additive can capture free acid in the electrolyte, and prevent hydrofluoric acid generated by the reaction of the silane groups and fluoroethylene carbonate with higher content in the electrolyte, so that corrosion of SEI (solid electrolyte interface) on the surfaces of positive and negative electrode particles is avoided, and the service life of a battery is prolonged.

In order to better understand the above technical solution, the following describes the above technical solution in detail with reference to specific embodiments.

Example 1

The embodiment provides a preparation method of lithium ion battery electrolyte, which comprises the following steps:

Preparing lithium ion battery electrolyte in a glove box filled with argon (oxygen content is less than or equal to 5ppm and water content is less than or equal to 10 ppm), wherein the organic solvent is Ethylene Carbonate (EC), propylene Carbonate (PC), methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC), diethyl carbonate (DEC), fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) and 1, 2-tetrafluoroethyl-2, 3-tetrafluoropropyl ether (HFE), and the organic solvents are uniformly mixed in sequence according to the mass ratio of 6:8:17:8:17:44 respectively. Wherein the mass percentage of the 1, 2-tetrafluoroethyl-2, 3-tetrafluoropropyl ether (HFE) is 35 percent of the electrolyte.

Then adding lithium salt, namely lithium bis (fluorosulfonyl) imide (LiFSI), into the mixed solution, wherein the mass of the lithium salt accounts for 22% of the total mass of the electrolyte, and stirring the mixed solution uniformly and fully dissolving the mixed solution. And adding auxiliary additives after the mixed solution returns to room temperature, wherein the auxiliary additives are Vinylene Carbonate (VC) and lithium difluoroborate (LiODFB) which respectively account for 0.5% and 2.0% of the total mass of the electrolyte.

And finally, adding a film forming additive into the mixed solution, wherein the structural formula of the film forming additive is shown in a formula (II), and the dosage of the film forming additive accounts for 1 weight percent of the total mass of the lithium ion battery electrolyte, and fully stirring and uniformly mixing the film forming additive.

Film-forming additives of formula (II) are commercially available from Li Fu Biotechnology.

The prepared electrolyte is used for preparing a lithium ion battery, and the specific steps are as follows:

And taking the prepared electrolyte, taking the electrolyte, injecting the electrolyte into a soft-package battery with the design capacity of 5 ampere hours, and carrying out vacuum packaging. The anode of the soft-packed battery is made of a nickel-cobalt-manganese ternary material, and the cathode of the soft-packed battery is made of a silica ink mixed material. And then the battery is subjected to the procedures of shelving, formation, aging, capacity division and the like in sequence, so that the lithium ion battery can be prepared.

Performance test:

The following performance tests were performed on the products of the examples and comparative examples:

1. And (3) testing the cycle performance, namely taking the lithium ion battery to be respectively placed in constant temperature environments of 25 ℃ and 45 ℃, and carrying out charge-discharge cycle test by using 1C0/1C0 (C0 is the capacity of the battery core), and recording the capacity retention rate and the cycle times.

2. And (3) a cycle resistance (DCR) growth test, namely taking a cell subjected to the cycle test at 25 ℃, placing the cell for 1 hour in a fully charged state, and then performing constant current discharge at a 1C1 multiplying power, wherein the cut-off condition is that the discharge capacity reaches 0.5 xC 1Ah. After the mixture is placed for 1 hour, constant current discharge is carried out for 10 seconds at a 5C1 multiplying power, and after the mixture is placed for 40 seconds, constant current charge is carried out for 10 seconds at the 5C1 multiplying power. After the constant-current discharge is carried out for 60 minutes by using a 1C1 multiplying power until the lower limit voltage is 2.5V, and after the constant-current constant-voltage charge is carried out for 10 minutes by using the 1C1 multiplying power until the upper limit voltage is 4.25V, the cycle test is continued. The test was performed once before the start of the cycle, and then once every 50 cycles, where C1 is the last discharge capacity before the test.

The results of the performance tests of the products of the above examples and comparative examples are shown in Table 1.

Table 1 results of performance testing of examples and comparative products

From table 1, it can be seen from the analysis of the test results of examples 1, 2 and 3 that the lithium battery exhibits excellent cycle performance and electrochemical performance when the film forming additive of the structural formula (II) (example 1), the film forming additive of the structural formula (III) (example 2) or the film forming additive of the structural formula (IV) (example 3) of the present invention is used, and that the cycle capacity retention rate of the lithium battery is higher and the ohmic resistance of the battery is more stable due to the stronger binding effect of the free acid when the structural formula (II) is used.

From the test results of example 1, comparative example 1 and comparative example 2, it was found that when the amount of 1, 2-tetrafluoroethyl-2, 3-tetrafluoropropyl ether was reduced, the amount thereof was 20% by mass of the electrolyte, and was less than 30% (comparative example 1), the reactivity was reduced due to the failure of formation of the desired solvation structure in the electrolyte, and no CIP was induced to form a lithium fluoride-rich SEI layer, resulting in poor cycle capacity retention of lithium batteries and poor ohmic resistance of batteries. When 1, 2-tetrafluoroethyl-2, 3-tetrafluoropropyl ether is not added (comparative example 2), the viscosity of the electrolyte is too high and the ionic conductivity is lowered, except that an ideal solvated structure is not formed, resulting in poor cycle capacity retention rate of the lithium battery and poor ohmic resistance of the battery. In summary, the test results of comparative example 1, comparative example 1 and comparative example 2 revealed that the lithium battery prepared from the electrolyte solution having a low amount of hydrofluoroether or no hydrofluoroether exhibited poor cycle capacity retention and battery ohmic resistance.

Comparative example 1 and comparative example 3 the cycle capacity retention and the battery ohmic resistance of the lithium battery prepared from the electrolyte of example 1 of the present application were comparable to those of the lithium battery prepared from an electrolyte in which lithium bis-fluorosulfonyl imide (LiFSI) accounts for 40wt% of the total mass of the electrolyte of the lithium ion battery.

From table 1, comparison of the test results of example 1 and comparative example 4 shows that the electrolyte of the present invention includes the film forming additive shown in the structural formula (II), and the obtained lithium battery still has a high capacity retention rate and a stable ohmic resistance of the battery after being subjected to charge and discharge cycles of 200 cycles and 200 cycles at 25 ℃ and 45 ℃ respectively, thereby exhibiting excellent electrochemical performance and cycle stability. When the film forming additive represented by the structural formula (II) was not added (comparative example 4), the surface of the positive electrode material was not protected, and the free acid in the electrolyte could not be suppressed, resulting in poor cycle capacity retention rate of the lithium battery and poor ohmic resistance of the battery.

As can be seen from analysis of the test results of example 1, comparative example 5, comparative example 6 and comparative example 7, when the film forming additive represented by structural formula (II) was used in an amount of 0.4wt% based on the total mass of the electrolyte solution for lithium ion batteries (comparative example 5), the ideal SEI layer could not be formed on the surface of the positive electrode due to the excessively low concentration, resulting in poor retention of the cycle capacity of the lithium batteries. When the additive represented by the structural formula (II) is used in an amount of 5.5% or 6.0% of the total mass of the lithium ion battery electrolyte (comparative example 6 and comparative example 7), since the positive electrode SEI layer is already formed, the redundant additive cannot continue to react, and thus the cycle capacity retention rate of the lithium ion battery is not further improved.

As a result of analyzing the test results of example 1 and comparative example 8, it was found that when the lithium salt mass ratio of the electrolyte was reduced to 11.5% (comparative example 8), the lithium salt concentration was too low to function to change the solvation structure, and a lithium fluoride-dominant SEI layer could not be formed, resulting in poor cycle capacity retention rate of the lithium battery and poor ohmic resistance of the battery.
